notes.body: @cnotin - can you see what the intention was here?  Should the assignment and check at line 2521 be for stored_packet_ntlmssp_info?  It has been this way for a long time...

Thanks for catching this. I introduced it in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10474/ (but I guess you already found that :wink:)

What I can say for sure is that functionally, NTLM decryption was broken before and now it's working.

Regarding the change, indeed it's a bit strange since I didn't want to change too many things. Basically the idea is to:

> skip decrypting the verifier, just storing its encrypted value. Then when the payload decryption is called, decrypt it, then call the function to finally decrypt the verifier. So the verifier is always decrypted after decrypting the payload, and before decrypting the next payload from the next request.

But indeed this removal: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10474/diffs#8d9cb24f56e210d8a3b8df941f84c5bd09e55ba8_2502_2528 makes it so `stored_packet_ntlmssp_info` is always NULL, so the following check just below is pointless:

```plaintext
if (stored_packet_ntlmssp_info != NULL && stored_packet_ntlmssp_info->verifier_decrypted == TRUE) {
```

Should we remove it perhaps?
I removed the test and unindented the else part - is that what you meant?
